learning_outcomes.text: Develop active speaking skills and the ability to communicate confidently in the contexts of university study, individual specialization, and future professional employment.
Systematically review and deepen key grammatical structures in more complex, authentic contexts.
Develop the ability to formulate ideas independently and communicate with confidence, preparing for more demanding academic and professional communication situations.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. U1: University study. Present and past tenses.
U1: Interview advice. Collocations with get, take, do.
U2: Watch to learn. Present perfect and past simple. Prepositions.
U2: Facts or fiction. Narrative tenses. Time linkers.
U2: Telling a story. Say, tell. Sequencers.
U3: Planning and procrastination. Talking about future plans.
U3: Future inventions. Making future predictions. Future time markers.
U4: Jobs. Personal qualities. Expressing obligation with must, have to, should.
U4: Dream job. Adjectives. Confusing words.
U4: Founding a start-up. Reaching agreement and managing a discussion.
assessment_rules: Students must take a credit test at the end of the semester. A minimum of 24 points out of a maximum of 40 points is required for the credit. Active participation in seminars and completion of optional activities may contribute up to 4 points to the credit. In case of failure, students have one resit opportunity for the test. Attendance at seminars is compulsory, with a maximum of two allowed absences; extra absences may be made up after consulting with the teacher.
